verdict.rationale: The skills ship their own SKILL.md descriptions that read like task-context triggers, such as understand-project-yylo activating "before planning or implementing a requested change". Skills use user-intent-first names, and the validator checks "invocation contracts", which points to deliberately engineered activation. However, nothing documents that skills fire automatically from context. Some evidence points the other way: single-letter manual shortcuts, and a Ralph loop that runs only on an "explicitly assigned" task. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of automatic context-based activation, a description-engineering or trigger-design rationale, and hands-on evidence that the right skill activates at the right moment.
